name: SIGMA - Domain Group Discovery via Net.exe [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/proc_creation_win_domain_group_discovery.yml (issue #217). The Sigma rule is already level:low (single-event, no timeframe, floods on help-desk/IAM administration) and stays that way for hunting/correlation - a single deliberate execution by an attacker still needs to be recorded. This threshold rule adds the higher-severity signal for what actually distinguishes automated recon tooling from routine account administration: domain group enumeration executed repeatedly on the SAME host within a short window. security-auditor review (#393): this rule's "from": "now-11m" / "interval": "10m" carried the same flat +1-minute-overlap shape as the other threshold rules in this corpus, undocumented here, with the identical mathematical gap - a real sliding 10-minute window is fully contained in a single 11-minute run window only 10% of the time for an arbitrary-phase campaign. Corrected to "from": "now-20m" (lookback >= interval + the 10-minute detection window), which GUARANTEES full containment. Cost: the effective counting window widens from 11 to 20 minutes and duplicate-alert risk across overlapping runs is not independently verified against multiple real Kibana scheduled runs.
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: A help-desk or IAM administration script that legitimately enumerates domain groups more than once against the same host in a short window.
